title: Eliminating Diesel Heaters from Electric Buses: A Two-Stage Mixed-Integer Optimization of Fleet, Charging, and Grid Planning in Cold Climates: reproduction package
description: Code, inputs and results for a two-stage scenario-based mixed-integer model that plans battery-electric bus fleets in cold climates. The model chooses, for each bus, a diesel cabin heater or electric heating only, together with battery size, depot and terminal chargers, and grid connection, and dispatches heat and charging over weather bands built from 24 winters of Toronto temperature records. It is applied to Toronto Transit Commission Route 52 (37 vehicle-days) and to the Arrow Road division (14 routes, 248 vehicle-days), with instances built from the scheduled weekday service of the public timetable feed. Contents: (1) model and campaign scripts (Python, Gurobi 11); (2) processed, non-confidential inputs: schedules derived from the public timetable feed, heating and traction model coefficients, weather band counts, tariffs and cost parameters; (3) complete result files and solver logs for the cost-emissions frontier, the sensitivity runs, the heater-price runs, the single-day benchmarks and the four division plans; (4) the out-of-sample reliability test (1,000 sampled days per weather band, three outcomes) with per-draw results; (5) scripts that regenerate the tables and figures of the paper. The trip-level telemetry of the Toronto Transit Commission is not included and cannot be redistributed; the empirical models estimated from it are provided, so every optimization result can be regenerated without the raw data. This version (v3.0.0) holds the v11 campaign and its tightening runs, which are the results reported in the manuscript submitted to Transportation Research Part C; results of earlier versions are superseded.
